result:
I've written the design for experiment 15 to `runs/pending_experiment.json`, and it parses as valid JSON. Nothing has been built or trained yet; the implementation agent and the training run come next.

**What changes:** the 128 px camera frame gets enlarged to 224 px inside the model before the borrowed ImageNet MobileNetV3 layers read it. Nothing else changes: same weights, no new parameters, same model size (7.45 MB), and the input and output of the exported model stay the same.

**Why:**
- Experiments 12, 13 and 14 are the only ones in this era that improved results on the held-out 2024 photograph, and each did it by leaning harder on the pretrained layers. Usable fixes on that photograph went from 10.75% to 49.5%, then 60.25%, then 65.5%.
- The training photographs are already at 95–97% usable. The check on how similar the model's description of a place looks across surveys barely moved between 13 and 14, so the remaining gap is the trunk still describing each photograph rather than the ground.
- Those layers learned their features on 224 px images, and we have been feeding them 128 px. Every roof and street looks 0.57× the size they were trained on. Their deepest layer is also a tiny 4×4 map, so one car or shadow that differs between surveys controls a sixteenth of the place description.
- Enlarging the frame matches the scale they learned at and makes those maps 14×14 and 7×7, which waters down one-off differences between surveys. A mismatch between training and use resolution is a known, large effect for pretrained layers (the FixRes paper, 2019). No experiment in either database has tried input scale.

**Prediction:** usable fixes on 2024 rise from 65.5% to 70–76%, false fixes stay at or below 5%, and the mission score drops from 0.395 to roughly 0.29–0.34.

**How it could fail:** if usable on 2024 stays at or below 66% while the training photographs hold, scale isn't the bottleneck. In that case the next move is more or different pretrained capacity, not resolution.

**Cost:**
- The pretrained layers do about 3× the computation.
- The host latency estimate goes from about 4 ms to 12–15 ms, against the 250 ms limit.
- Training on the AWS g6 goes from about 17 min to an estimated 40–50 min.
- Latency on the chip itself should also roughly triple. That's worth measuring but acceptable at a fix every 1–10 s.

The implementation brief limits edits to `Member.embed` plus logging. It restates the CLI and model-file contracts and the rule that nothing under `model/` may open the 2024 photograph.
